data.title: Corgi Insurance hires former Chubb Underwriting AVP James Kullman
data.description:
Corgi Insurance hires former Chubb Underwriting AVP James Kullman

Corgi Insurance hires former Chubb Underwriting AVP James Kullman

PR Newswire

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 16, 2026

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Corgi Insurance today announced the appointment of James Kullman as Head of Underwriting, North America. Kullman brings nearly 15 years of experience in commercial insurance underwriting and management, with expertise spanning risk assessment, portfolio management, product development and underwriting strategy.

Kullman joins Corgi from Chubb, where he most recently served as Assistant Vice President and Pacific North Region Underwriting Manager for North American Small and Lower Middle Market. His previous experience includes underwriting roles at CNA Insurance, The Hartford and Liberty Mutual, where he worked across construction, middle-market accounts and property and casualty insurance.

At Corgi, Kullman will lead efforts to advance commercial underwriting across North America, leveraging AI to improve risk selection, develop underwriting guidelines, strengthen portfolio management and support regulatory compliance. His role will focus on combining traditional underwriting expertise with AI-assisted tools and processes to help make commercial insurance more efficient, responsive and accessible.

"Commercial insurance has relied on many of the same processes for decades. AI gives us an opportunity to rethink how underwriting works, from how we evaluate risk to how quickly we can deliver a quote," said James Kullman, Head of Underwriting, North America at Corgi. "I'm excited to bring my experience in traditional underwriting to a team that is building new technology and infrastructure for the industry."

Corgi is building a full-stack insurance platform that combines proprietary underwriting technology with in-house claims handling and insurance infrastructure. By bringing underwriting expertise and AI together, the company aims to help businesses get coverage more efficiently while maintaining disciplined risk selection and strong underwriting standards.

Kullman's appointment reflects Corgi's continued investment in insurance expertise as it expands its commercial insurance capabilities and builds technology designed to modernize how carriers, brokers and customers interact.

About Corgi Insurance

Corgi is an AI-native insurance carrier built for high-growth companies. The company combines proprietary underwriting technology, in-house claims handling, and modern insurance infrastructure to deliver coverage built for the way businesses operate today.

data.title: VCI Global Advances AI Infrastructure and Token Services Strategy; Strengthens Balance Sheet in 1H2026
data.description:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- VCI Global Limited (NASDAQ: VCIG) (“VCI Global” or the “Company”), today announced its unaudited financial results for the six months ended June 30, 2026 (“1H2026”), as it advances its strategic transition toward AI computing, AI token services and infrastructure-related opportunities.

The first half of 2026 marked a significant transition for VCI Global following the separation and divestment of its capital markets consultancy, fintech and other non-core businesses. The Company is now concentrating its resources and capital allocation on building AI computing capabilities, commercializing AI services and developing infrastructure opportunities across the AI value chain.

At the same time, VCI Global is pursuing complementary opportunities in renewable energy, energy storage and carbon assets as it works toward a broader infrastructure model connecting AI, computing, energy and sustainability.

  • Total equity increased 19.2% to US$114.70 million as of June 30, 2026, compared with US$96.21 million as compared to December 31, 2025.
  • Total liabilities declined 17.7% to US$17.03 million from US$20.69 million over the same period.
  • Cash and bank balances rose more than fivefold to US$5.19 million from US$0.94 million, supported by financing activities and the disposal of an investment.
  • Revenue was US$2.56 million, compared with US$18.74 million in 1H2025, reflecting the Group’s portfolio restructuring and changes in its operating profile.
  • VGAIN Compute was launched, providing customers with a platform to purchase AI tokens and access multiple supported large language models, including OpenAI GPT, Kimi, Meta Llama and Qwen.
  • Acquisition of the controlling stake in PT Fine Carbon Credit Indonesia (FCCI), an Indonesian carbon asset platform associated with approximately 241,000 hectares of forestry areas across four project sites.

“The first half of 2026 represents an important inflection point for VCI Global as we reposition the Company around AI infrastructure and scalable technology services,” said Ang Zhi Feng, Chief Financial Officer of VCI Global. “While revenue declined as a result of the transition, we ended the period with higher total equity, lower liabilities and an increased cash balance. Our priority is to manage liquidity carefully and allocate capital to initiatives with clear commercial potential as we advance our AI services and infrastructure strategy.”

REVENUE REFLECTS PORTFOLIO RESTRUCTURING

The first half of 2026 represents a fundamental change in VCI Global’s operating profile.

The Company has completed the separation and divestment of its capital markets consultancy, fintech, and other non-core businesses, reducing exposure to businesses that were not aligned with its longer-term technology and infrastructure strategy.

Revenue for 1H2026 was US$2.56 million, compared with US$18.74 million in 1H2025. The decrease primarily reflects businesses that have since been separated or divested, along with the transition to a more focused AI infrastructure and technology operating model.

The Company recorded a net loss of US$8.43 million in 1H2026, compared with net profit of US$4.66 million in 1H2025. The change reflects the Company’s revised operating profile following portfolio restructuring, together with changes in revenue and expenses. The Company continues to develop its AI and technology initiatives, with future performance dependent on commercial adoption and execution.

Cost of services declined 97.1% to US$104,641 from US$3.66 million in the prior-year period. The reduction primarily reflects the divestment of the business consultancy subsidiary in 2025 and the completion of several large-scale technology projects in the prior period.

Consultant fees were nil, compared with US$251,622 in 1H2025, following the divestment of the business consultancy subsidiary. IT expenses decreased to US$55,767 from US$3.29 million, as new technology projects remained in their initial rollout stages during the period.

These lower expenses reflect the Group’s changed business structure and project cycle. They should not, on their own, be interpreted as evidence of improved profitability, as the Company’s financial performance will also depend on future revenue generation and the costs associated with scaling its new businesses.

CASH POSITION AND CAPITAL ALLOCATION

As of June 30, 2026, total equity increased 19.2% to US$114.70 million from US$96.21 million at December 31, 2025, while total liabilities declined 17.7% to US$17.03 million from US$20.69 million.

Cash and bank balances increased to US$5.19 million from US$0.94 million at year-end 2025. The increase was supported by financing activities and the disposal of an investment.

The Company intends to prioritize capital deployment based on commercial demand, financing availability and project readiness, with investment priorities spanning AI Infrastructure, GPU computing and related infrastructure.

VGAIN COMPUTE: FROM AI ACCESS TO AI CONSUMPTION

VCI Global announced the launch of VGAIN Compute on October 6, 2026, through its subsidiary V Gallant Limited.

The platform enables users to purchase AI tokens to access supported large language models, including OpenAI GPT, Kimi, Meta Llama and Qwen. Announced applications include content generation, coding, research, business applications and workflow automation.

The platform introduces a customer-facing offering through which VCI Global can pursue revenue from AI services. Its token-based model provides a mechanism for charging users for access to supported AI capabilities.

The broader market opportunity is expanding as businesses move AI from experimentation into production. Gartner forecasts worldwide AI-optimised IaaS spending of US$42.3 billion in 2026, rising to US$66.1 billion in 2027. Gartner also estimates that global spending on AI inference infrastructure will reach US$23.3 billion in 2026, exceeding the US$19 billion forecast for AI model training infrastructure.

The Company’s next priorities include expanding platform usage, evaluating additional models and developing enterprise and developer applications.

DEVELOPING AN INTEGRATED POWER–AI–CARBON ECOSYSTEM

VCI Global’s longer-term infrastructure strategy extends beyond computing capacity to the resources required to support the expansion of AI infrastructure, including electricity generation, solar power, energy storage and data center operations.

The Company intends to develop an integrated infrastructure model designed to connect energy supply with computing demand, with the objective of improving power availability, supporting scalable AI computing and enhancing long-term operating efficiency.

As AI workloads become increasingly compute-intensive, access to reliable and scalable power is becoming an increasingly important consideration in the development of data center and GPU infrastructure. VCI Global believes that combining computing infrastructure with energy development can provide greater control over critical infrastructure requirements as its AI businesses expand.

LONGER-TERM OPPORTUNITIES IN ENERGY AND FOREST CONSERVATION

VCI Global announced that V Gallant had entered into a definitive agreement to acquire a 70% stake in PT Fine Carbon Credit Indonesia (FCCI), a platform associated with approximately 241,000 hectares of forestry areas across four project sites in Indonesia.

The proposed acquisition provides a potential basis for developing forestry-linked carbon credit projects, subject to transaction completion and applicable technical, legal and regulatory requirements.

The voluntary carbon market offers a potential monetization route for eligible forestry projects, but credit prices vary significantly according to project type, certification standard, carbon integrity, vintage, and buyer demand.

According to Ecosystem Marketplace’s 2025 State of the Voluntary Carbon Market report, based on 2024 transactions, the average price was approximately US$14.97 per tonne of CO₂ equivalent for improved forest management credits and US$20.44 for tree-planting and restoration credits. Some premium credits may command prices above US$50, depending on their characteristics and market conditions.

COMMERCIAL PRIORITIES AND INVESTOR MILESTONES

VCI Global’s initiatives cover several potential sources of revenue, each with different development requirements.

  • AI services: VGAIN Compute provides a live platform through which the Company can pursue paid AI model access. Commercial performance can be assessed through active paying users, token consumption, revenue and service delivery costs.
  • GPU cloud services: VGAIN Cloud is intended to support demand for AI computing. Relevant milestones include infrastructure deployment, available GPU capacity, customer contracts, utilisation and revenue generated from computing services.
  • AI data center infrastructure: Galatron AI Factory’s initial planned 5MW deployment provides a defined development milestone within the broader 500MW roadmap. Progress will depend on site readiness, power availability, funding and customer demand.
  • Energy infrastructure: Potential revenue opportunities depend on the development and ownership of specific projects, available generation or storage capacity, and contracted demand.
  • Carbon assets: FCCI represents a potential forestry-linked carbon credit opportunity. Key milestones include transaction completion, project qualification, credit issuance and actual sales.

These indicators provide a clearer basis for evaluating the Company’s progress than global market growth alone.

OUTLOOK

The global expansion of AI infrastructure presents opportunities across model access, cloud computing, data center development and supporting energy infrastructure. VCI Global has announced initiatives across these areas, beginning with the launch of VGAIN Compute and extending to planned computing infrastructure and complementary asset opportunities.

The Company’s ability to benefit from these markets will depend on execution and commercial validation. Market forecasts indicate the scale of industry investment, but they do not establish VCI Global’s future revenue, market share or profitability.

VCI Global intends to progress its initiatives in phases, with the commercial outcomes of each business dependent on customer demand, operating performance, capital availability, project milestones and applicable regulatory requirements.

“Our ambition is to build an AI infrastructure business that connects customer demand, computing capacity and the energy required to support it,” said Victor Hoo, Group Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman of VCI Global. “VGAIN Compute provides a commercial entry point for building customer relationships and recurring usage, while our infrastructure strategy creates opportunities to participate more deeply in the AI value chain. Over the longer term, we see the potential to develop an integrated model in Asia that brings together AI computing, energy and forest conservation.”

“We intend to demonstrate the value of this transition through execution. That means growing customer usage, bringing productive computing capacity into service and converting commercial opportunities into revenue. Those are the milestones that will define the next phase of VCI Global.” He added.

Management will continue to emphasize commercial validation, disciplined capital allocation and phased execution. The pace of development and contribution from individual initiatives will depend on customer demand, funding, regulatory considerations and project milestones.

About VCI Global Limited

VCI Global Limited is transforming into an AI infrastructure and technology group focused on AI computing, GPU infrastructure and AI token services through its businesses, including V Gallant and VGAIN Compute. Following the spin-off and divestment of its capital markets consultancy, fintech and other non-core businesses, the Company is sharpening its focus on AI-driven growth while exploring complementary opportunities in renewable energy, power generation, energy storage and forest conservation, including potential carbon credit initiatives. Through these interconnected areas, VCI Global aims to build a scalable and sustainable infrastructure platform supported by disciplined capital allocation and long-term value creation.

data.title: ShimmerScreen(R) Custom Metal Chain Curtains Create Statement Chandelier and Doorway Feature at Vaseline's New York City Pop-Up
data.description:
MOUNT VERNON, NY / ACCESS Newswire / October 16, 2026 / ShimmerScreen®, the architectural metal curtain division of Ball Chain Manufacturing Co., Inc., was featured at Vaseline's date night pop-up event in New York City on September 18, 2026. Designed by experiential creative agency Mirror NYC, the event incorporated custom decorative metal ball chain into two distinctive installations: a multi-layered chandelier and a walk-through doorway curtain. Special recognition goes to Eduardo Perez of Mirror NYC for his work on the project.

Manufactured in Mount Vernon, New York, ShimmerScreen's architectural metal chain curtains provided a versatile design solution that brought color, texture, and movement to the immersive brand experience. The installations demonstrate how custom metal chain can be incorporated into overhead decorative features, interactive entrances, and architectural partitions, offering designers creative flexibility for temporary events and experiential environments.

Custom Red and Pink Metal Ball Chain Creates a Statement Chandelier

At the center of the event space, a custom chandelier featuring 3/16" Ball-Bar Epoxy Painted Steel ShimmerScreen in deep red and light pink created an eye-catching, multi-layered fringe installation. Suspended from custom circular track, the decorative metal chain formed a sculptural centerpiece that complemented the event's rose-toned walls and pink and red accents.

The Ball-Bar chain style introduced additional texture and visual interest, while the layered arrangement created depth throughout the installation. As the metal chain interacted with the surrounding lighting, the chandelier added a shimmering effect that enhanced the event's playful atmosphere.

The installation highlights ShimmerScreen's ability to create customized chandelier-style architectural features using a range of chain sizes, styles, finishes, and track configurations.


Light Pink Metal Chain Curtain Creates an Interactive Entrance

In addition to the chandelier, a custom doorway curtain featuring 3/8" Round Powder Coated Steel ShimmerScreen in light pink provided a decorative transition between areas of the event.

Suspended from a straight track, the metal ball chain curtain introduced an interactive element as guests walked through the strands. The installation helped define separate areas while maintaining visibility, airflow, and an open atmosphere.

Unlike traditional solid partitions or doors, ShimmerScreen's flexible metal chain curtains allow guests to move directly through the installation, making them an engaging design feature for experiential events, retail activations, and entertainment spaces.

American-Made Metal Chain Curtains Offer Customization for Experiential Design

The Vaseline pop-up event highlights the versatility of ShimmerScreen's custom architectural metal chain systems for experiential marketing, brand activations, and temporary installations.

"Working with the Mirror NYC team on the Vaseline pop-up was a great opportunity to show what ShimmerScreen can bring to an experiential space," said Bill Taubner Jr., Executive Vice President of ShimmerScreen. "What made this installation especially exciting was seeing the material customized around such a distinct creative vision and become an integral part of the environment. That ability to transform ShimmerScreen for a particular brand or experience is a big part of what makes these collaborations so rewarding for us."

Backed by nearly 90 years of American manufacturing expertise through Ball Chain Manufacturing Co., Inc., ShimmerScreen offers architects, interior designers, and experiential agencies direct access to its manufacturing capabilities. From custom Pantone-matched colors and a wide selection of metal finishes to straight, circular, and custom-curved track systems, each installation can be tailored to the project's specific design requirements.

ShimmerScreen's architectural metal curtains can be incorporated into decorative chandeliers, ceiling installations, room dividers, entrances, backdrops, and other statement features. The product's versatility makes it an ideal solution for pop-up events, trade shows, retail displays, hospitality spaces, and permanent architectural installations.

To explore custom metal chain curtain applications, browse the ShimmerScreen project galleries or request samples and a project quote.

About ShimmerScreen®

ShimmerScreen® creates custom decorative metal chain curtains, architectural room dividers, privacy screens, window coverings, ceiling features, lighting elements, and screening solutions for commercial and residential environments.

Originally conceived in 2002 by Bill Taubner Sr., ShimmerScreen reimagined traditional metal ball chain as an architectural design material. Today, its installations can be found in hotels, corporate headquarters, casinos, airports, restaurants, retail stores, entertainment venues, healthcare facilities, sports arenas, and residences worldwide.

Manufactured in the United States by Ball Chain Manufacturing Co., Inc., ShimmerScreen combines design flexibility with established manufacturing expertise. Each installation is produced to the specifications of its project, helping architects and designers define spaces while preserving light, visibility, airflow, and openness.

Learn more at www.ShimmerScreen.com.

About Ball Chain Manufacturing Co., Inc.

Family-owned since 1938. American-made for nearly 90 years.

Founded by a father and son in a small garage in the Bronx, New York, Ball Chain Manufacturing Co., Inc. has grown into the world's largest manufacturer of metal ball chain and the only manufacturer of metal ball chain in the United States.

Now in its fifth generation of family leadership, the company manufactures millions of feet of ball chain each week at its 70,000-square-foot campus in Mount Vernon, New York. Its products serve customers throughout North America and around the world across architecture, interior design, military, government, aerospace, industrial, retail, medical, and consumer markets.

Ball Chain has proudly supplied the iconic military dog tag chains worn by generations of United States service members, reflecting a longstanding commitment to quality and dependable manufacturing.

In addition to ShimmerScreen®, the company's divisions include LogoTags®, which provides custom challenge coins, military coins, medals, dog tags, and promotional products. Across its businesses, Ball Chain combines the personal attention of a family-owned company with the manufacturing experience, innovation, and responsive service customers need to move their projects forward.

data.title: Alignment Healthcare Investigation Initiated: Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC Investigates the Officers and Directors of Alignment Healthcare, Inc. - ALHC
data.description:
Alignment Healthcare Investigation Initiated: Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC Investigates the Officers and Directors of Alignment Healthcare, Inc. - ALHC

Former Attorney General of Louisiana, Charles C. Foti, Jr., Esq., a partner at the law firm of Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC (“KSF”), announces that KSF has commenced an investigation into Alignment Healthcare, Inc. (“Alignment” or the “Company”) (NasdaqGS: ALHC).

On July 8, 2026, reports emerged that a former Alignment executive had filed a whistleblower lawsuit alleging that the Company deliberately misclassified $8 million to $10 million in routine operating expenses as capital expenditures to boost its stock price and executive compensation. According to the lawsuit, this maneuver artificially inflated the Company’s adjusted EBITDA and allowed it to report its “first full year of positive adjusted EBITDA as a public company.” Then, on September 15, 2026, at the Baird Global Healthcare Conference, Kao declined to comment on the Company’s Star Ratings positioning, stating, “I cannot talk about it at all[.]” On October 8, 2026, Alignment disclosed that CMS had downgraded the Star Rating for its H3815 contract to 3.5, making the plan ineligible for quality bonus payments in fiscal 2028. Following these disclosures, the Company’s share price declined precipitously.

KSF’s investigation is focusing on whether Alignment’s officers and/or directors breached their fiduciary duties to its shareholders or otherwise violated state or federal laws.

If you have information that would assist KSF in its investigation, or have been a long-term holder of Alignment shares and would like to discuss your legal rights, you may, without obligation or cost to you, call toll-free at 1-833-538-3606 or email KSF Managing Partner Lewis Kahn (lewis.kahn@ksfcounsel.com), or visit https://www.ksfcounsel.com/cases/nasdaqgs-alhc/ to learn more.

data.title: KBRA Assigns Preliminary Ratings to Angel Oak Mortgage Trust 2026-6 (AOMT 2026-6)
data.description:
KBRA Assigns Preliminary Ratings to Angel Oak Mortgage Trust 2026-6 (AOMT 2026-6)

KBRA assigns preliminary ratings to ten classes of mortgage-backed certificates from Angel Oak Mortgage Trust 2026-6 (AOMT 2026-6), a $250.6 million non-prime RMBS transaction. The underlying collateral, comprised of 381 residential mortgages, and includes a meaningful concentration of collateral that KBRA considers to be “non-prime.” All the loans are either classified as non-qualified mortgages (62.8%) or exempt (37.2%) from the Ability-to-Repay/Qualified Mortgage rule due to being originated for non-consumer loan purposes. Angel Oak Mortgage Solutions originated 65.0% of the pool, with no other originator comprising over 10% of the collateral.

KBRA’s rating approach incorporated loan-level analysis of the mortgage pool through its Residential Asset Loss Model (REALM), an examination of the results from third-party loan file due diligence, cash flow modeling analysis of the transaction’s payment structure, reviews of key transaction parties and an assessment of the transaction’s legal structure and documentation. This analysis is further described in our U.S. RMBS Rating Methodology.

data.title: Utilities Up on Defensive Bias — Utilities Roundup

data.title: Nowhere to hide: Tech selloff hits software and chip stocks alike
data.description:
By Hannah Pedone

The software and semiconductor sectors haven't been trading in tandem much this year, but they collectively fell Friday as AI and interest-rate fears hit the market

Shares of Salesforce closed down 2% on Friday amid a broad-based selloff in the technology stocks.

Even the software sector wasn't immune from a broad-based technology selloff in the stock market Friday.

Investors had been rotating into the software sector earlier in the week, deeming these stocks to be compelling alternatives to highflying chip stocks that were seen as more vulnerable to concerns about the sustainability of artificial-intelligence spending.

But semiconductor and software stocks fell in tandem on Friday, leaving tech investors with nowhere to hide. The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector exchange-traded fund IGV, a proxy for the software sector, closed down 4.8%, while the iShares Semiconductor ETF SOXX was off 4.1%.

Within the software sector, ServiceNow's stock (NOW) finished down 4% and Oracle's stock (ORCL) closed 5% lower. Shares of Salesforce (CRM) lost 2% on the day, while Twilio's stock (TWLO) was the S&P 500's SPX biggest loser with its 10.6% decline.

D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria told MarketWatch that what used to be a negative correlation between chip stocks and software stocks is "no longer a major factor in the market." He said that Friday's broad-based technology selloff was "not leaving any stock untouched."

"Investors no longer view AI progress as bad for software and are treating individual software companies based on their specific prospects," he said.

Morningstar analyst Luke Yang told MarketWatch there wasn't one single factor gripping the market on Friday, as investors seemed to be digesting a broad breakdown of faith in the AI trade this week.

The "wide range of potential outcomes" for companies tied to the AI trade has made it difficult for investors to maintain faith in AI-exposed stocks, he said - whether it be the indebted neocloud provider CoreWeave (CRWV), chip giant like Nvidia (NVDA) or software and cloud company Oracle (ORCL).

Cybersecurity stocks were also caught up in the software selloff on Friday after Palo Alto Networks (PANW) - which sells firewall products to corporate customers - released an advisory disclosing a security vulnerability earlier this week. The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, which lies within the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, added Palo Alto Networks to its catalog of known security vulnerabilities.

The Amplify Cybersecurity ETF HACK closed down 4% on Friday, with Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) shares each falling more than 7%.

One issue could be the specter of interest-rate hikes, which affects technology companies across the board that have to borrow money.

The "data-center buildout requires capital which is becoming more expensive," Luria said, as higher rates mean higher funding costs for companies investing heavily in AI infrastructure.

Software stocks are also sensitive to rate hikes as their valuations are often tied to cash flows years into the future, and higher interest rates change the way those are valued. And many software companies need to borrow money as well.

Financial-technology stocks may be feeling the pain as well from fears of an imminent rate hike, as higher rates mean higher default risk for lenders, Mizuho anlayst Dan Dolev told MarketWatch.

Speaking Friday at the International Monetary Fund and World Bank Group's annual meeting in Bangkok, Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh declined to share any expectations for the central bank's upcoming rate-setting meeting.

See also: The murky AI milestone that has some of the industry's leading voices increasingly on edge

-Hannah Pedone
